sentences.text:
Mukesh Chandrakar S/o Shri Avan Chandrakar Aged About 34 Years At -
 Rasni, Police Station Aarang, District - Raipur, Chhattisgarh.

---- Applicant
 Versus
 State Of Chhattisgarh Through Sho Police Station Mahila Thana, District
 Durg, Chhattisgarh.

---- Respondent
 For the Applicant : Shri Faiz Kazi, Advocate.

For the Respondent/State : Shri Shakti Singh, P.L.
 Hon'ble Shri Justice Rakesh Mohan Pandey
 Order
16.02.2023
1.
With the consent of both the parties, the application is heard finally at motion stage itself.

I.A.
No.1 of 2022, an application for grant of interim relief is disposed of.

2. This is the first bail application filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant who is apprehending arrest in connection with Crime No. 107 of 2022, registered at Police Station - Mahila Thana, District - Durg, Chhattisgarh for the offences punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. As per prosecution story, the marriage between the applicant and the complainant was solemnized on 10.3.2016 and after 6 years, the complainant "wife" lodged FIR making allegation of harassment, cruelty with demand of dowry against the present applicant and his family members.
On such complaint, the police registered the offence punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of the IPC.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that there is one daughter from their wedlock and after 6 years, false allegations have been leveled against him and his mother, father, brother and wife of brother.
He would further submit that the other co-accused persons have already been extended benefit of Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. by the Court below.

He would also submit that there are general allegations against all the accused persons and considering the allegations leveled against the other co-accused persons they have been extended benefit of Section 438 of the Cr.P.C.
Mukesh Chandrakar vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119548452/
1 and on the ground of parity, the applicant is also entitled for the same.
5. On the other hand, learned State counsel opposes the bail application and the submissions made in this respect.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary with utmost circumspection.
7. From the case-diary, it appears that the marriage between the applicant and the complainant was solemnized on 10.3.2016 and the FIR has been lodged on 2.11.2022 and there is one daughter from their wedlock and the other co-accused persons have already been extended benefit of Section 438 of the Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Mukesh Chandrakar vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering the further fact that the allegations are almost similar against all the accused persons, I am inclined to allow this bail application.
8.
Accordingly, the bail application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Cr.PC. is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest of the applicant in connection with the aforesaid offence, he shall be released on bail by the Officer arresting him on executing a personal bond in sum of Rs.50,000/-
with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer.

Sd/-
